post.description:
Merges `source` into `target` (defaults to `main`). Outcome is one of
`already_up_to_date`, `fast_forward`, or `merged`. Returns 409 with the
list of conflicts if the merge cannot be completed; the target is left
unchanged in that case. **Destructive** to `target` on success. `commit`
carries this merge's own target publication, including for a fast-forward;
an already-up-to-date merge returns `commit: null`.

With `dry_run: true` the merge stops after classification and validation:
the response reports the outcome it would have now (`commit: null`,
`dry_run: true`), a conflict answers the same 409, and nothing is written.
A dry run is a read of both branches and needs no `branch_merge` grant.

With `delete_branch: true` the source branch is deleted after a successful

`branch` selects which history to list: a named branch returns the history
reachable from that branch's head (the main commits inherited up to the
fork plus the branch-authored commits); omitting it returns `main`'s
history. There is no cross-branch listing. Ordering is part of the
contract: newest first along the branch's first-parent chain, which is
falling generation and falling (graph-manifest version, created-at, commit
id). Read-only.

(`head_commit_id`) and continues with `next_page_token`, sent back as
`page_token` with the same `branch`; later pages answer for that head's
chain even after the branch moves. A page reads only the history it
returns. Without `limit` and `page_token` the whole history is one answer.

commit of `branch`'s history: one the branch still holds or a readable
branch published costs nothing more; any other is looked for down the
branch's history, which costs what the whole listing costs, and a commit
the history does not reach is refused (400).

target is `branch` (writes `as commit` awaiting `commit publish`), newest
first; each carries `published: false`. `unattached=true` lists instead
the live unattached snapshots whose recorded target is `branch` (writes
`as unattached branch`), newest first, each with `kind: "unattached"`;
the two filters together are refused (400), as is either with `limit` or
`page_token`.

Designed for ad-hoc exploration and AI-agent tool-use: short field
names (`query`, `name`) match the CLI `-e` flag and the GQ `query`
keyword. Mutations (`insert`/`update`/`delete`) are rejected with 400
-- use `POST /mutate` for writes. Select a branch or snapshot and obtain
the pinned graph-commit token with the response. Cedar authorizes Read for
read queries and Change for `explain load csv`.

The GQ statement `branch list` is also served here, with no `branch`,
`snapshot`, `name`, or `params`: it answers one result per branch (field
`name`, byte order) under the same `read` check as `GET /branches`. So are
the branch control reads, each under its route's checks and errors:
`branch diff <source> [into <target>]` and `branch diff <from> to <to>`
(one result per entity change, fields `kind`, `type`, `id`, `op`,
`before`, `after`; the compared commits and the continuation token in
`page`; `after page "<token>"` and `limit <n>` continue and bound it),
`branch merge-base <source> [into <target>]` and
`branch merge <source> [into <target>] dry run` (one result each).
`branch create`, `branch delete`, and `branch merge` are rejected with
400; send them to `POST /mutate`.

The GQ statement `explain query …` is served here too: the query is not
run, and the result describes its v2 logical, physical and available
DataFusion trees, one result per node (fields `tree`, `depth`, `node`, `detail`), followed by
`plan` entries for the passes and the document's other fields, under the
request's target and `params`. `explain load csv …` answers the accepted
load plan the same way (`logical_initial`, `logical`, `physical`, then
`plan` entries), under the request's `branch` alone. It requires the load's
Change decision before probing the external source's metadata; it reads
no payload byte and publishes nothing.

BlobPreconditionFailureOutput.description:
A Blob write's `If-Match` did not hold for the cell (HTTP 412). The write
had no effect. `current_etag` is the cell's validator when it holds a
managed value; it is absent for a null or external value, which no tag
matches. Distinct from [`PreconditionFailureOutput`], the graph-commit
precondition.

BlobRangeOutput.description:
Normalized half-open range details for an unsatisfiable managed Blob read.

HTTP also returns `Content-Range: bytes */N`; these fields let SDKs inspect
the failure without parsing either that header or the human-readable text.

BlobWriteOutput.description:
Receipt of a Blob put or clear.

null, with neither. The `etag` is the one a read at `commit` reports.

describes one.

branch was created, or the commit `from_commit` named. For a commit
start, `from` is the branch that wrote the commit.

from.description:

from_commit.description:

deleted; `false` when the deletion was refused or failed (the merge
itself still succeeded — see `branch_delete_error_details`).

oneOf.description:
This merge's own publication, including for a fast-forward. Always
present on the wire; `null` only when already up to date.

dry_run.description:
`true` for a dry run: `outcome` is what the merge would do now, and
`commit` is `null` because nothing was written.

as_commit.description:

the target head is unchanged until `commit publish`. Refused together
with `delete_branch`, whose source the proposal still holds.

under its own `branch_delete` policy check; a refusal or failure is
reported via `branch_deleted` / `branch_delete_error_details` on the response
and never fails the already-landed merge.

response reports the outcome the merge would have now, a conflict
fails with the same `409` a merge returns, and nothing is written.

`delete_branch`.

A merge conflict has no kind: it is the 409 `POST /branches/merge` answers.

BranchStartRefusalOutput.description:
A branch create refused at the graph commit `from_commit` named; nothing
was created.

branch.description: For `branch_deleted`, the branch that wrote the commit.

type_name.description: For `not_retained`, the graph type whose stored version cleanup reclaimed.

BranchStartRefusalReason.description: Why a branch could not start at the graph commit `from_commit` named.

ChangeBaselineOutput.description:
Terminal payload of a baseline stream: the captured snapshot commit and
the cursor that resumes the feed immediately after it.

ChangeBaselineRecord.description:
Wire envelope of the FINAL baseline stream line: `{"baseline": {...}}`,
distinguishable from snapshot records (which carry `type`/`edge` keys).
Emitted exactly once, only after every snapshot record — an interrupted
stream has no terminal record and therefore no usable cursor.

ChangeBaselineRequest.description: Body for the change baseline handshake.

kind.description:
Feed scope the resume cursor is bound to. The snapshot honors `kind`
and `type`; `op` constrains only subsequent polls.

ChangeBlockOutput.description: One commit block inside a feed page.

ChangeCauseOutput.description: The commit cause of one change block, stated once.

authored_at.description:
Authorship time as Unix epoch microseconds — minted before dataset
effects and stable across retries; deliberately not labeled a commit or
publication time.

authored_branch.description: The branch the commit originally landed on (not the requested branch).

ChangeDiffRefusalOutput.description: A well-formed entity-diff request this commit cannot satisfy (HTTP 409).

type_name.description: The graph type at the schema boundary, when the reason names one.

ChangeDiffRefusalReason.description: Why a well-formed entity-diff request was refused (HTTP 409).

ChangeEndpointsOutput.description:
Edge endpoints as graph references. Endpoints belong to each image, so an
endpoint-moving update has distinct before and after endpoints.

ChangeErrorOutput.description:
Error envelope for the read-only change surfaces (`…/changes`,
`…/changes/baseline`, `…/commits/{commit_id}/changes`): a wire-compatible
projection of [`ErrorOutput`] restricted to the graph-vocabulary details
those routes can produce after their error projection. The write-path
conflict shapes (key / published-dataset-version / merge / read-set) are
structurally absent because change routes cannot produce them. Servers
serialize [`ErrorOutput`]; every field a change route can populate appears
here with the same name and meaning, and absent optionals are wire-compatible.

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 409 when a commit entity diff is refused (parentless
commit or an unprovable schema boundary).

Set with HTTP 410 when retained history can no longer reconstruct a
change continuation. Recover via the baseline handshake.

code.description: The failure's registry code, as on [`ErrorOutput`].

disposition.description: What the request did and what to do next, as on [`ErrorOutput`].

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 503 when the graph has a durable recovery intent that
must be resolved before the requested change read can proceed.

Set when a requested limit exceeds a public ceiling, or a single change
exceeds the poll's own byte ceiling.

ChangeFeedGapOutput.description:
A change continuation can no longer be reconstructed from retained history
(HTTP 410), sent with [`ErrorCode::ChangeFeedGap`]. Recovery is the
baseline handshake; retrying the same cursor cannot succeed.

caught_up.description:
Present with `cursor` on a terminal page: true when the page reached
its captured head, false when more complete commits already wait.

cursor.description:
Durable caller-owned cursor, advanced only over complete commits and
returned only on a terminal page — an interrupted poll never advances
it.

next_page_token.description: Continue this poll's captured cut. Absent on a terminal page.

ChangeImageOutput.description: One exact logical entity image, decoded with the commit-era schema.

oneOf.description: Present for edge images only.

properties.description:
Exact logical property values, user-schema keys verbatim; a null cell
keeps its key, an absent key was outside that commit's schema.

ChangeOpOutput.description:
Logical operation of one change. Ordering rank is frozen:
insert before update before delete within one entity.

affected_edges.description: Edges the mutation touched, under the `affected_nodes` rule.

affected_nodes.description:
Nodes the mutation touched. Not reported for a branch statement,
which moves refs, not nodes or edges: `0` whenever `outcome` is present.

branch.description:
The branch that received the effect, or the recorded target of an
unattached write (a child inherits its base's target whatever the
request named). For a branch statement: the created branch, the
deleted branch (gone by the time this is read), or the merge target.

oneOf.description:
This write's own publication, including for a fast-forward merge.
Always present on the wire; `null` for branch creation, deletion, or
an already-up-to-date merge, which publish no graph content commit.
Present only when the request was a branch statement.

query_name.description:
The declared mutation's name, or a branch statement's two keywords
(`branch create`, `branch delete`, `branch merge`).

name.description: Name of the mutation to run when `query` declares multiple.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the mutation's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ mutation source containing `insert`, `update`, or `delete` statements.
May declare multiple named mutations; pick one with `name`. May instead
be one branch statement (grammar: `BranchStmt` in `omnigraph-compiler`),
sent with no `name`, `params`, or `branch`.

oneOf.description: Session settings for this request (the Session settings RFC); see [`SettingsRequest`].

ChangeTypeOutput.description:
Graph-scoped type identity. `id` is opaque: it survives a supported rename
and changes after drop/re-add. It is not a type-name selector or path.

CommitChangesOutput.description: One bounded page of the finite commit entity diff.

next_page_token.description:
Continue THIS bounded response. Absent on the final page. Never a feed
cursor.

CommitKindOutput.description:
`published`: a commit of a branch's lineage. `unpublished`: a proposal
(`as commit`) awaiting `commit publish`. `unattached`: an unattached
snapshot (`as unattached branch`), which never publishes.

head_commit_id.description:
The head a paged listing's first page resolved; every later page
answers for its first-parent chain and repeats it as its page token
carries it, unchecked. Present only when the request set `limit` or
`page_token`.

next_page_token.description:
Continue THIS listing below the last commit of the page. Absent on the
last page and on an unpaged listing.

created_at.description: Commit creation time as Unix epoch microseconds.

kind.description:
Which kind of commit this is. Required on the wire; a legacy receipt
without it derives `published` or `unpublished` from `published`.

published.description:
`false` for an unpublished commit (a write `as commit`) or an
unattached snapshot (a write `as unattached branch`): readable by its
id, invisible to every branch read; only the former publishes.
`graph_manifest_version` is then the detached version holding it.
Always `kind == published`.

root_commit_id.description:
The root of an unattached snapshot's chain, the snapshot's own id on
a root; `null` for the other kinds.

DiagnosticOutput.description:
The diagnostics contract for a refused query (RFC 0047): a stable code
(`Q…` parse, `T…` typecheck); where the failure is, as a source position
or as the stage and expression when it is post-parse; what was expected or
violated; and one concrete fix, absent when `expected` names the decision.
Rides `ErrorOutput.diagnostic` as an additive detail because
[`ErrorCode`] is a closed compatibility contract.

DiffOutput.description:
One bounded page of a graph diff: the net entity changes between two
resolved commits, in the commit diff's entity shape and order. There is no
cause: a range has no single author.

base_commit_id.description: The merge base, present only for a branch diff.

from_commit_id.description:
The commit the `from` side resolved to; for a branch diff, the merge
base.

next_page_token.description:
Continue THIS bounded response; later pages answer for the same two
commits. Absent on the final page.

to_commit_id.description:
The commit the `to` side resolved to; for a branch diff, the source
head.

DispositionOutput.description:
What a refused or failed request did and what its caller should do next.
A server states it on every error response, computed where that knowledge
is; a client that lost the response knows less, and says so.

EntityChangeOutput.description:
One entity change. Cause is stated once on the enclosing block, never here.
An insert carries only `after`, an update exact `before` and `after`, a
delete only `before`.

ErrorCode.description:
The registry of error codes. A server sends each code under the HTTP statuses named with it; a code without one never appears in an HTTP response.

- `unauthorized` (401): The request carries no credential the server accepts: a bearer token is missing, unknown or expired. Supply one the server is configured to verify.
- `forbidden` (403): The credential's actor may not do this: policy denies the action, or the action needs a policy permit the server has not been given.
- `bad_request` (400): The request is malformed or invalid: a body, query string, path parameter or header that does not decode, a query the compiler refuses (see `diagnostic`), or a value refused before any effect.
- `api_contract_mismatch` (400): The request lacks exactly one `Omnigraph-Http-Api` header naming the contract this server speaks. Authentication and this check precede graph access and effects.
- `actor_mismatch` (412): The request's `Omnigraph-Expect-Actor` header names another actor than its credential resolves to. Nothing ran.
- `outcome_unknown` (500): A write whose completion the server could not settle: it may or may not have published. Read the target before writing again; never replay the write blindly. An MCP write call that was cancelled or passed its deadline answers it too.
- `precondition_failed` (412): A request precondition no longer holds: the branch head moved past `Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit` (see `precondition_failure`), or a Blob's `If-Match` names a value the cell no longer holds (a write's `blob_precondition_failure` names the current one). Nothing was written.
- `recovery_required` (503): An overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved first; see `recovery_required`.
- `external_blob_source` (424): An admitted external Blob source could not be probed or read; see `external_blob_source`.
- `change_feed_gap` (410): Retained history can no longer reconstruct a change continuation; see `change_feed_gap`. Resume from a new baseline.
- `not_found` (404): The graph, branch, commit, query, entity or route the request names does not exist, or the caller may not learn that it does.
- `method_not_allowed` (405): The request path is served, but not with the request's method.
- `request_timeout` (408): The request body did not arrive before its deadline; nothing was admitted.
- `conflict` (409): The request conflicts with the graph's current state: a concurrent change, an existing id, a merge conflict, an index that must be built first, or a commit that cannot be diffed. The details say which.
- `branch_start_refusal` (409, 410): `branch create` could not start the branch at the commit `from_commit` named, and nothing was created; see `branch_start_refusal`, whose `not_retained` reason answers 410.
- `unattached_cannot_publish` (409): The commit is an unattached snapshot, a kind that never publishes. Distinct from `conflict`, the authority-moved refusal of a publishable proposal.
- `payload_too_large` (413): The request body, or the work it asks for, exceeds a bounded limit; `resource_limit` names the limit when it is the operation's. Split or reduce the request.
- `unsupported_media_type` (415): The request body's content type is not one the route accepts.
- `range_not_satisfiable` (416): The requested Blob byte range lies outside the value; see `blob_range`.
- `too_many_requests` (429): Admission capacity is exhausted: an actor's, the server's, or the MCP endpoint's concurrent tool calls. Nothing started; retry after `Retry-After`.
- `service_unavailable` (503): Operation admission is closed, or a deployment observation raced an owner change. Nothing started; retry after `Retry-After`, reconciling any earlier write first.
- `graph_unavailable` (503): A known graph is not being served. The request did not start, so it may be retried once the graph is served again.
- `internal` (500): The server failed. An error before any write took no effect; see the server log.
- `cancelled` (no HTTP status): MCP only: the client cancelled a read tool call. A cancelled write answers `outcome_unknown`.
- `deadline_exceeded` (no HTTP status): MCP only: a read tool call passed its deadline. A write that does answers `outcome_unknown`.
- `result_too_large` (no HTTP status): MCP only: a tool result exceeds the result limit. Narrow the read.

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 412 when a Blob write's `If-Match` did not hold for the
cell. The `ETag` response header repeats `current_etag` when present.

Set with HTTP 416 for a valid but unsatisfiable managed Blob byte range.
`start..end` is half-open and `length` is the selected Blob length.

Set with HTTP 409, or 410 for `not_retained`, when `branch create`
cannot start a branch at the commit `from_commit` named.

Set with HTTP 409 when a commit entity diff is refused (parentless
commit or an unprovable schema boundary).

Set with HTTP 410 when retained history can no longer reconstruct a
change continuation. Recover via the baseline handshake.

code.description:
The failure's registry code. Servers set it on every error response; it
is absent only from a body built outside a server.

oneOf.description:
Set for a refused query: the diagnostics contract's code, position or
stage, expectation and fix. `error` keeps the one-line rendering.

disposition.description:
What the request did and what to do next. Servers set it on every error
response; it is absent only from a body built outside a server.

oneOf.description:
Set with HTTP 424 and `external_blob_source` when an external Blob URI
passed admission policy but its source could not be probed or read.

Set with HTTP 409 when a selected full-text index requires an explicit
rebuild before search can succeed. Unlike a write-authority conflict,
this condition is not cleared by retrying. This additive discriminator
preserves the closed [`ErrorCode`] contract.

Set when a strict keyed insert found an existing or concurrently
inserted logical id.  The caller may choose a different id; replaying
the same strict operation will not convert it into an upsert.

Set with HTTP 412 and `precondition_failed` when a mutation's
graph-commit precondition failed.

Set when the conflict is a publisher CAS rejection. The caller's
pre-write view named the expected published dataset version, but the
graph manifest now publishes the actual version. Refresh and retry.
Set when a prepared write's logical authority changed before effects.

Set when an overlapping durable recovery intent must be resolved before
retry. Its dataset effects may or may not have started.

Set when the request must be split into smaller graph commits. The
rejected attempt has no durable effect.

type_names.description: Restrict the export to these node/edge type names. Empty exports all types.

ExternalBlobSourceOutput.description:
Structured details for an allowed external Blob source that could not be
probed or read, sent with [`ErrorCode::ExternalBlobSource`].

reason.description:
Source-side failure diagnosis. Clients should branch on the presence of
`external_blob_source`, not parse this human-readable text.

uri.description: Normalized, credential-free URI spelling (or a redacted placeholder).

FullTextIndexRebuildRequiredOutput.description:
A selected full-text index cannot safely serve the current analyzer (HTTP 409).
This is not a retryable write conflict: an operator must rebuild the live
branch's indexes. Historical snapshots stay unchanged; branch old content
and rebuild that branch to search it.

reason.description:
Human-readable diagnosis; branch on the enclosing detail's presence,
not this text, to distinguish the operator-action-required condition.

FullTextIndexRequiredOutput.description:
A full-text call read a declared full-text index that has no segment at
the query's snapshot (HTTP 409), so no segment carries its analyzer. This
is not a retryable conflict: an operator builds the branch's index
(`omnigraph optimize` on main, `omnigraph rebuild-full-text-indexes
--branch` elsewhere). Historical snapshots stay unchanged.

GraphBatchDeclarationOutput.description:
One logical declaration touched by a graph-batch load.

This deliberately carries the accepted-schema name, not a backing dataset
selector, path, or Lance identity.

GraphBatchLoadOutput.description: Terminal result for the raw graph-level NDJSON load surface.

base_branch.description:
Base branch a fork was requested from, even when the target already
existed. `null` when the request omitted `from`.

edges.description: Logical edge declarations touched by this batch, sorted by name.

oneOf.description:
`unsupported` when a loaded node type declares `@embed`, including
when all vectors were supplied; `null` otherwise.

nodes.description: Logical node declarations touched by this batch, sorted by name.

GraphDiscoveryEntry.description: A graph's existence, without storage, schema, data, or serving metadata.

display_name.description: Currently the graph identifier; no separate display name is configured.

GraphInfo.description:
One entry in the response from `GET /graphs`. Cluster operators
consume this list to discover which graphs the server is currently
serving. This legacy metadata includes the storage `uri`; identity-only
existence discovery uses [`GraphDiscoveryEntry`] instead.

read_available.description: Runtime availability; actor policy still gates every operation.

GraphListResponse.description:
Response from `GET /graphs`. Lists every graph registered with the
server in alphabetical order by `graph_id` (sorted server-side so
clients get deterministic output across requests).

GraphStartupFailure.description: Bounded startup classification, without storage paths or error text.

internal_schema_version.description:
The internal-schema (storage-format) version this binary writes, the
highest it serves. Normal open serves every version from the binary's
lowest supported one up to this one; a graph below that range is
refused until it is upgraded offline or rebuilt, and a graph above it
needs a newer binary.

base_branch.description:
Base branch a fork was requested from (the request's `from`), echoed
even when the branch already existed. `null` when `from` was absent.

edges.description: Logical edge declarations touched by this load, sorted by name.

oneOf.description:
`unsupported` when a loaded node type declares `@embed`, including
when all vectors were supplied; `null` otherwise.

nodes.description: Logical node declarations touched by this load, sorted by name.

branch.description:
Target branch. Defaults to `main`. Without `from`, the branch must
already exist — a missing branch is a 404, never an implicit fork.

data.description:
NDJSON payload: one record per line, each shaped
`{"type": "<TypeName>", "data": {...}}`.

from.description:
Parent branch used to create `branch` if it does not exist. Branch
creation is opt-in by presence of this field; omit it to require an
existing branch.

oneOf.description: How existing entities are handled. Defaults to `merge`.

InvokeStoredQueryRequest.description:
Body for `POST /queries/{name}` — invokes the server-side stored query
named in the path. The query source and name come from the registry,
never the body; only the runtime inputs are supplied here.

branch.description:
Branch to run against. Defaults to `main`; for a stored mutation the
write targets this branch.

expect_mutation.description:
The kind the caller expects: `Some(false)` for
`omnigraph query <name>`, `Some(true)` for `omnigraph mutate <name>`.
When set and it disagrees with the stored query's actual kind, the
server rejects the call (400) so the verb asserts the kind. `None`
(the default) skips the check — preserving older clients and aliases.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the stored query's declared parameters.

snapshot.description:
Snapshot id to read from (read queries only — rejected for a stored
mutation). Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

InvokeStoredQueryResponse.description:
Response for `POST /queries/{name}`: the read envelope for a stored
read, or the mutation envelope for a stored mutation. Serialized
**untagged**, so the wire shape is exactly [`ReadOutput`] or
[`ChangeOutput`] — classification follows the stored query, not a
wrapper field.

KeyConflictOutput.description:
A strict insert rejected because `entity_id` already names an entity in the
selected node or edge type. The refused write changed nothing; an earlier
step of the same request, such as the branch a load forks, may already have
published, which the error's `disposition` states. Partial or ambiguous
attempts surface `recovery_required` instead.

LoadEmbeddingGeneration.description: Load capability for a batch touching a node type with declared `@embed`.

LoadMode.description: Shadow enum for documenting [`LoadMode`] in the OpenAPI schema.

MergeBaseOutput.description:
The commit a merge of `source` into `target` would classify against, and
the two heads it was computed from.

ParamDescriptor.description: One declared parameter of a stored query, projected for the catalog.

oneOf.description:
Element kind when `kind == list` (always a scalar — the grammar
forbids lists of vectors or nested lists).

nullable.description: `false` → the caller must supply it; `true` → optional.

ParamKind.description:
The kind of a stored-query parameter, decomposed so a client (e.g. an
MCP server) can build a typed input schema with a closed `match` and
never re-parse omnigraph's type spelling. `bigint`/`date`/`datetime`/
`blob` are carried as JSON strings on the wire: a 64-bit integer past
2^53 loses precision as a JSON number, and Date/DateTime are ISO
strings, Blob a blob-URI string.

PositionOutput.description:
A source position: 1-based line and column (in characters) and the byte
offset.

PreconditionFailureOutput.description:
Structured details for a caller write-precondition failure: HTTP 412, a
mutation carried `Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit: <commit_id>`, and the branch
head no longer matches that id. The write had no effect; the caller re-reads
the branch and decides again. `actual` is `None` on a branch with no commits.

PublishedDatasetVersionConflictOutput.description:
Structured details for a publisher-level OCC failure. Surfaces alongside
HTTP 409 when a write was rejected because the caller's pre-write view of
one backing dataset's published version was stale relative to the current
head. The expected/actual fields tell the client which dataset to refresh.

QueriesCatalogOutput.description:
Response for `GET /queries`: every stored query in a graph's
registry, each with typed parameters.

QueryCatalogEntry.description: One entry in the stored-query catalog (`GET /queries`).

mutation.description: `true` for a stored mutation → an MCP read-only hint of `false`.

QueryRequest.description:
Inline read-query request for `POST /query`.

Mutations are rejected with 400 — use `POST /mutate` for write queries.
Field names are deliberately short (`query`, `name`) to match the GQ
keyword and the CLI `-e` flag.

branch.description: Branch to read from. Mutually exclusive with `snapshot`. Defaults to `main`.

name.description:
Name of the query to run when `query` declares multiple. Optional when
only one query is declared.

params.description: JSON object whose keys match the query's declared parameters.

query.description:
GQ read-query source. May declare one or more named queries; pick one
with `name` when more than one is declared. Mutations
(`insert`/`update`/`delete`) get 400 — use `POST /mutate` instead. May be the branch
statement `branch list` or a branch control read (`branch diff …`,
`branch merge-base …`, `branch merge … dry run`), sent with no `name`,
`params`, `branch`, or `snapshot`; or one `explain` statement (`explain query …`), which
answers the v2 plan instead of
running it, as one result per plan node (fields `tree`, `depth`, `node`,
`detail`: the logical, physical and available DataFusion trees, then `plan` entries for
the passes and the document's other fields), under the same `params`,
`branch`, or `snapshot` as the query itself. `explain load csv …` answers the accepted
load plan as the same results (`logical_initial`, `logical`, `physical`, then `plan`
entries), under `branch` alone: `snapshot`, `name` and `params` are refused.
It requires the load's `change` permission before probing source metadata,
reads no payload byte, and publishes nothing.

oneOf.description: Session settings for this request (the Session settings RFC); see [`SettingsRequest`].

snapshot.description: Snapshot id to read from. Mutually exclusive with `branch`.

graph_commit_id.description:
Effective graph head commit id of the exact snapshot this read was
served from. On a fresh named branch this is the inherited source head,
so it is immediately usable as `Omnigraph-If-Graph-Commit` (CLI:
`--if-commit`) for the branch's first conditional write. The id and rows
come from one pinned version, so no separate id fetch is needed.

oneOf.description:
Page state of a paged control read (`branch diff`); absent for every
other answer.

ReadPageOutput.description:
The page state a `branch diff` answer carries: the exact commits it
compares, and the token `after page "<token>"` continues it with, absent
on its last page.

base_commit_id.description: The merge base, for a branch's diff since it.

ReadSetConflictOutput.description:
Structured authority mismatch for a prepared write. Values are
strings because members include optional graph commit ids and future
authority tokens, not only numeric published dataset versions.

ReadinessOutput.description:
The readiness witness of one replica (`GET /readyz`, RFC 0049): whether
it is serving or draining, the applied revision it booted from, and how
many graphs it does and does not serve. Unauthenticated, so it carries
no graph id: those stay behind `GET /graphs`.

blocked_graph_count.description: Unavailable graphs outside startup, including closed transitions.

booted_serving_digest.description:
The `config_digest` of the applied revision this process booted from.
Fixed for the life of the process: the server never reloads.

loading_graph_count.description: Registered graphs waiting for their initial startup admission.

ready.description: False during shutdown or when a nonempty inventory has no ready graph.

ready_graph_count.description: Registered graphs whose startup completed successfully.

served_graph_count.description: Number of registered graphs, including blocked entries.

shutdown_grace_seconds.description: The bound on graceful shutdown, after which the process exits 2.

state_cas.description: The ledger CAS (`sha256:<hex>`) the process booted from.

state_revision.description: The ledger revision the process booted from.

ResourceLimitOutput.description:
A write rejected before durable recovery ownership because its bounded
physical plan exceeded an explicit entity, byte, or transaction-chain ceiling.

catalogue_source.description:
The engine catalogue's built-in `@` types as `.pg`-style
declarations, listed beside the graph's own schema: read-only rows
the binary derives from its registries, never part of the schema
source above. Optional for compatibility with servers predating it.

oneOf.description:
The graph's physical system column spellings: `__id`/`__src`/`__dst`
on current-vintage graphs, `id`/`src`/`dst` on legacy ones. This is
storage discovery for loaders, exports and raw readers of mixed
vintages; query results address identity and endpoints through the
meta-fields `@id`, `@src` and `@dst` on every vintage. Optional for
compatibility with servers predating the field.

SettingsRequest.description:
The `settings` field of a request: one optional value per `request`-scope
setting of the definition, applied to the request's session before the
source's own `set` lines, so a `set` line in the request's text overrides
the field. An absent field is empty. A `process` setting has no field
here, so `{"stage_write_concurrency": 64}` is refused as an unknown field.

ann_nprobes.description: the partition cap per index delta of a `nearest` scan; `0` is no cap

engine.description: the engine a read query runs on; `v2`, the plan runner, is the one value; this setting does not change change-feed or merge execution

history_release_bytes.description: the byte budget of a branch's buffer of unreleased commits; a mutate, load or branch merge of this session whose buffer and head reach it closes a history block and the publish after it writes the block under `__history`; query results never change, only where settled commits are stored and how many requests a publish makes

load_source_max_bytes.description: the largest object a `load csv` statement reads, checked before any payload byte is fetched; a served load is additionally bounded by the server's workload admission

merge_lineage.description: how a merge finds the entities it classifies: the full-scan walk, the lineage path, or both compared

query_memory_bytes.description: the memory pool one read query runs under, and the allowance one load statement's retained read-reuse buffers are admitted against; tracked work past it is refused, and a raised value is memory one query or load may hold

traversal_work_limit.description: the finite work budget shared by edge selections in one query; exhaustion terminates the query with an error

write_max_bytes.description: the byte allowance for bounded writes by mutate, load and branch merge; entity data and materialized Blob payloads each have this independent allowance; lowering it preserves the existing per-type, per-operation and per-chunk scopes; a value raised above the default is held in memory as one typed batch at commit

internal_schema_version.description:
The on-disk internal-schema (storage-format) version this graph's branch
is stamped at. It may be below the version the binary writes (the
`internal_schema_version` of `GET /healthz`): normal open serves a range
of versions, and a branch in that range takes the current one at its
first publish.

SuggestionOutput.description: Non-overlapping edits against the original request source.

TextEditOutput.description: A UTF-8 byte range in the original source, with an exclusive end.
